body: Underlying renewed calls for American empire is the assumption that flexing military might is the only way for the US government to respond to China and Russia's existence and influence

. This approach has costs— both monetary and nonmonetary—which must be considered. As the US government's experience with the war on terror indicates, extensive reliance on the military instrument has a high monetary price tag, with one estimate placing the total cost of post-9/11 wars at $8 trillion.2 These costs far exceeded initial government projections based on strategies of a similar sort to those proposed by current proponents of American empire to confront China and Russia—i.e., straightforward plans based on an array of favorable assumptions about interveners with promises of grandiose outcomes.
